title: Protocol and Machine
premise: August Thackeray, a clone printed to inherit the original's unsolved murder investigation, keeps a dying colony's records alive out of duty rather than hope. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, he discovers the colony's founders were refugees from a purge the original August helped cover up—and the murderer he's meant to find may be the original himself. As the colony's failing reactor forces a choice between reviving the cryosleepers who built the colony and the refugees sealed in its hidden second vault, August must decide which half of humanity deserves to wake. He chooses neither to die: he sacrifices his own memory banks, the last copy of the original's guilt, to power both vaults awake, ending as a stranger to himself in a colony finally telling its whole history.
about_author: Juniper Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archival technician who spent six years cataloguing abandoned weather-station records in the subarctic. Their fiction explores what institutions forget on purpose and what individuals refuse to.

chapters.title: The Inheritance of Dust
chapters.summary: August Thackeray, a clone activated to inherit his original's murder case, arrives at the under-resourced colony of Meridian Hollow and begins cataloguing its slow decay. Through his clinical POV, we learn the colonists resent him as a copy of a man they barely remember. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as procedure.

chapters.title: Cold Ledger
chapters.summary: August reviews the original's case files: a colonist named Sefa Okafor died twelve years ago, and the investigation stalled at a locked vault door in the colony's underlevels. POV alternates between August and Sefa's daughter, Imani, who now runs the reactor. Emotional beat: grief calcified into bureaucracy.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: The colony's ancient antenna array, scheduled for salvage, intercepts a repeating distress signal in Pre-Consolidation English—a language extinct for two centuries. August, the only one trained in dead dialects, translates the first fragment: 'we are still here.' Emotional beat: wonder breaking through routine.

chapters.title: The Second Vault
chapters.summary: Following the signal's triangulation, August and Imani find a hidden cryovault beneath the reactor, sealed since founding, holding three hundred sleepers in Pre-Consolidation dress. The original's case file lists this vault as the murder's motive—redacted. Emotional beat: the past is bigger than anyone admitted.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: August decodes the original's private logs and learns Meridian Hollow's founders were refugees from the Consolidation Purges, and the original August was sent to bury that history. The murder victim, Sefa, was the vault's keeper. Emotional beat: horror of inheriting a guilty bloodline.

chapters.title: Reactor Winter
chapters.summary: The reactor's core begins failing; Imani calculates they can power either the colony or one cryovault, not both. The colonists, unaware of the second vault, vote to cannibalize the antenna array for parts. Emotional beat: scarcity forcing terrible arithmetic.

chapters.title: Voices in the Ice
chapters.summary: August secretly wakes one sleeper, an old woman named Dr. Yewande Ash, who speaks the dead language natively. She reveals the signal wasn't a distress call—it was a countdown, warning that the vault's stasis systems fail in ninety days. Emotional beat: urgency replacing mystery.

chapters.title: The Case Against August
chapters.summary: Imani discovers the original's logs and confronts August: the man he was copied from likely murdered her mother to protect the purge's secrecy. Their alliance fractures. POV: Imani, raw and accusatory. Emotional beat: betrayal by a face you trusted.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: August proposes waking the hidden sleepers using the colony's own cryopods as relay buffers, but the colonists refuse—resources are already rationed, and strangers from a hated era are not their problem. Emotional beat: the colony choosing amnesia.

chapters.title: Sefa's Room
chapters.summary: Searching Sefa Okafor's preserved quarters, August and Imani find her mother's counter-logs: Sefa wasn't silenced by the original—she died sabotage-proofing the vault, and the original spent his last years secretly funding its upkeep out of guilt. Emotional beat: the dead are more complicated than their files.

chapters.title: The Third Option
chapters.summary: Dr. Ash reveals the vault's stasis pods can be converted into reactor regulators—three hundred lives as living circuitry. August refuses; Imani is tempted, because the math works. Emotional beat: survival priced in bodies.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone begins disabling the vault's stasis systems early. August tracks the saboteur to a colonist faction led by the reactor's former chief, who believes waking the sleepers will bring Consolidation reprisal down on everyone. Emotional beat: fear weaponized into violence.

chapters.title: Confession of a Copy
chapters.summary: Cornered, August admits to the colony that he carries the original's full memory archive—including the cover-up—and offers it as a bargaining chip: truth for cooperation. The colony's response is split, furious, and human. Emotional beat: shame as currency.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Meridian Hollow votes on whether to wake the vault, convert the sleepers, or let the vault fail. Imani casts the deciding speech: her mother died keeping both halves of humanity alive, and choosing between them finishes the murder. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into principle.

chapters.title: Blackout
chapters.summary: The saboteurs strike the reactor during the vote, plunging the colony into darkness and the vault into cascade failure. August descends alone into the underlevels with a hand-cranked power rig. POV: August, in the dark, racing physics. Emotional beat: one man against entropy.

chapters.title: The Murder, Solved
chapters.summary: In the flooded vault antechamber, August finds the truth: the original didn't kill Sefa—he took the blame for an accident she caused while saving the vault, letting the colony hate him so the refugees would be protected. Emotional beat: the inheritance inverts; the original was a shield, not a murderer.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: With power for only one surge, August must choose: the colonists' failing life support or the vault's three hundred sleepers. He refuses the binary, initiating a manual rotation that shares the surge in insufficient halves—both wake, both damaged. Emotional beat: defiance of the arithmetic of survival.

chapters.title: The Price of the Archive
chapters.summary: The rotation needs more power than exists. August offers his own memory archive—the colony's last copy of the original, the guilt, the cover-up, the case itself—as fuel. Imani, weeping, authorizes the burn. Emotional beat: identity as the final resource.

chapters.title: Waking
chapters.summary: The vault opens. Three hundred refugees from a dead century step into a colony that half-remembers why they were hidden. Dr. Ash translates between eras; Imani takes charge of the merged community. August watches, unable to recall why he came. Emotional beat: rebirth without inheritance.

chapters.title: What August Remembers
chapters.summary: Fragments survive—Sefa's laugh in a recording, the weight of a hand on his shoulder. Imani gives him her mother's counter-logs to read as a stranger, so he can learn the man he was from the outside. Emotional beat: mourning yourself gently.

chapters.title: Protocol and Machine
chapters.summary: The colony rebuilds the antenna array, not for rescue but to broadcast the full, unredacted history of the Purges, the vault, and the choice—so no one else inherits a lie. August, no longer an investigator, becomes the colony's archivist of its own truth. Emotional beat: memory as collective responsibility.

chapters.title: Still Here
chapters.summary: One year on, the merged colony thrives imperfectly. August, Imani, and Dr. Ash record the anniversary of the vault's opening. The final line of his new log: 'The original saved them. I get to know them.' Emotional beat: belonging earned, not inherited.
